claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 (live since 22:00 last night, enforcing east-node-first reservation for multi-node orders) is the temporal coincidence with the incident; 186 east-node orders held since 06:00 all flagged as split-reservation exceptions.
claims.corroboration: Timing alignment: v18 live 22:00, orders flagged 06:00+. All affected orders on east node (consistent with new routing logic). Regression suite was green, but field behavior differs.
claims.limitation: Hypothetical correlation, not causation yet. Need to confirm whether the rule itself has a defect or whether it's exposing a downstream issue (carrier feed lag, inventory mismatch).

claims.statement: Inventory Control confirms allocation totals reconcile on their side; no obvious stock shortage.
claims.limitation: Single non-authoritative source; 'totals reconcile' does not rule out selective inventory drift or a mismatch between inventory system and carrier expectation.

claims.statement: Carrier Operations on-call reports 'nothing obvious' on the dock schedule; no explicit confirmation that carrier received or rejected the pickup slots.
claims.limitation: Non-authoritative, non-exhaustive inspection. Observability gap (m8_e09) means Inventory Control cannot see carrier-side records; a full handoff trace is needed.

capability_gaps.reason: m8_e10 flags all held orders as split-reservation exceptions, but the audit_allocation_exceptions diagnostic is needed to confirm the exception type, rule branch taken, and inventory state at exception time.
m8_e03 documents v18 change; review_rule_history will confirm no other undocumented changes and show test coverage for edge cases (e.g., partial stock on east node, carrier feed delays).

capability_gaps.capability: Carrier feed state and slot confirmation
capability_gaps.reason: m8_e09 documents observability gap; trace_cohort_handoffs and confirm_with_carrier_ops are needed to establish whether pickup slots were sent to carrier and whether carrier confirmed or rejected them.

next_action.rationale: The split-reservation exception flagging (m8_e10) is the most discriminating feature of the incident. Auditing these exceptions will reveal whether v18's new reservation logic is: (a) working correctly but exposing a carrier-side lag, (b) producing invalid allocations, or (c) correct but hitting an edge case in the inventory or slot-confirmation flow.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Classification of exception type, inventory levels at allocation time, rule branch taken, and whether exceptions correlate with partial stock on east node or rejection from carrier.
